column1: # Targeted verdict queue — one request per line:
#   <40-char sha>
# The watcher drains these FIRST among its idle phases. A request is satisfied
# when that sha has a verdict at that tier, so lines need no deletion and a
# repeat is a no-op. Stale lines cost one archive lookup per cycle; tidy at
# will, but nothing breaks if you never do.
# STRUCK 2026-08-28 by frank-coordinator, unserved: the ab51855df full request.
# It asked for the pin COMMIT; the question was about the pin TREE 83468c5462d4,
# which verify_pin answered on its own at 2026-08-27T23:25:33Z (RED, 0 new).
# The request was never read — the resident daemon predated the draining code —
# so serving it now would spend a 3202-job full tier, on the box that is the
# binding constraint, at a sha 20+ testable commits stale, to re-answer an
# answered question. Always --covering first, and check whether an existing
# phase already produces the verdict before queueing.
# STRUCK 2026-08-30 by frankT, unserved: the 440c822e6a80 full request.
# CONTAMINATED, not stale — it is a real sha and it does carry the -O2 promotion,
# but `merge-base --is-ancestor 72b4c47a7 440c822e6a80` is NO, so it carries
# frankB's broken string-literal commit 9588c8535 WITHOUT its revert. A full
# tier there returns RED with the ~24 nilpy jobs frankwasm traced to 9588c8535,
# and those reds land in a row keyed to the promotion — an archive row that
# outlives the session that knows better. Two string-literal-handle changes 36
# minutes apart, one broken, and the target contained both. Naming a SHA when
# the question is about a TREE STATE is the mistake; check what a target
# contains, not only that it exists.
# Replaced by 1d8db8667, verified here to contain 440c822e6 AND 72b4c47a7.

column4: -O2 default changed for every lane: EmitStaticLitHandle(+A64) promoted -O3->-O2. Post-revert target — contains the promotion 440c822e6 AND the revert 72b4c47a7, so a red here is attributable. EXACT native at this sha is RED with new_red=[] (one pre-existing job, test_warn_ignored_directives), so native is already answered: what is unserved is CROSS, and the aarch64 arm moved in the same commit and has only been run under qemu by its author. Watch in-place literal mutation and two evaluations assumed distinct.

Shared-IR control-flow rewrite blocking a pin held on an ABSENCE, not a red: IRMarkReachableLabels replaces IRMarkReferencedLabels and IROptDeadCode's own fixpoint is deleted, touching every backend. Verified here: c9a1f6f2a IS an ancestor of f370bb085, so ONE verdict covers both -- they are one risk, not two. TIER IS full DELIBERATELY, and the requester offered a downgrade I am declining: the question is 'does a control-flow rewrite break any CROSS target', and `limited` is BY CONSTRUCTION the no-qemu tier (see TIERS in tools/testmgr.py -- 'the cross variants stay in full', and test-float-determinism is excluded precisely to keep limited runnable on a box without qemu). So limited answers 0% of the question. It would also be near-pure duplication: the sampler already has THREE native runs at descendants (0b930abf9 GREEN, 4e883063f GREEN, ff0799098 RED with new_red=[test_pointer_to_a_named_fixed_array] -- unrelated to control flow), so the native half is largely answered and full's entire marginal value here is the cross matrix. NOT overtaken: 0 runs at this exact sha and no descendant tested above native. If the sampler reaches it at full before you drain this, strike the line rather than serving it.
